title: BPP continuity_root_update request (DESIGN.md §7.3, §14.8; registry R13 participant) — v2 (G10/G31 rebound)
description: Mutation (meta required); an update — meta.expected_revision carries the last observed revision (§14.2, registry rule). Single owning-Participant operation for the whole ContinuityRoot lifecycle (§14.8: absent → active; active → active(new revision), sealed, or retired; sealed → retired), discriminated by target_status with head CAS via meta.expected_revision — a derivation, gap note G11. continuity_root_ref is absent exactly on first adoption. Byom need not see the plaintext; undeclared influence receives the most restrictive label (§7.3). V2 SUCCESSOR (RT-06): the G10/G31 opaque bodies of the immutable v1 publication are rebound here — every authority-bearing field is a canonical BPA-1 expression, a closed protocol shape, or an exact digest-pinned reference (DESIGN.md §14.7; ADR-0001 landing note). Executable-looking members (callback, regex, ...) fail the closed AST. B1 and C3a freeze to this version; v1 stays published and unchanged.

compatibility_selector.description: Canonical BPA-1 policy value (ADR-0001; RT-06 G10/G31 rebinding): the compatibility selector.

identifier.description: Opaque visible-ASCII identifier, at most 128 bytes (§14.9).

safeNonNegativeInteger.description: I-JSON safe integer (§14.2 rejects unsafe integers).

timestamp.description: RFC 3339 UTC instant with Z offset, semantically valid in the proleptic Gregorian calendar: the pattern pins the lexical ranges and implementations MUST additionally reject impossible calendar instants (e.g. 2026-02-30) — the conformance runner enforces this on every vector; leap seconds are not accepted. DESIGN.md does not fix a timestamp wire encoding; this derivation freezes with the bundle (gap note G3, amended per RT-17).

digestRef.$comment: The closed family DigestRef wire (family-vectors/PROFILE.md §6.1, normative; D-R0-1): exactly the members {class, algorithm, key_ref?, value_hex}. The oneOf pins the closed class/algorithm pairing and requires key_ref exactly for the keyed erasure classes; each arm refines members of this already-closed object.

class.description: Digest class (PROFILE.md §6, D-R0-1); substituting one class where a schema requires another is a conformance failure.

key_ref.description: Key id for the keyed erasure classes; raw HMAC keys, per-object secrets, and salts are never part of a DigestRef.

digestRef.description: Typed DigestRef: every digest field is typed, never an unlabelled hash. Wire shape, class/algorithm pairing, and key_ref presence per the ratified family profile.

mutationMeta.description: MutationMeta (§14.2). Required on every mutation; this operation is update-classed (current-head CAS), so expected_revision — the last observed revision of the exact record head the operation moves — is REQUIRED (closed update meta; RT-01). Omitting it fails the closed schema; the server compares it against the current head and a stale value fails stale_revision.

rules.description: Bounded rule set (§14.9 BPA policy-node cap, pinned at 256 pending registry freeze). Rule order is not semantically significant (deny-wins is order-free); canonical form sorts rules by JCS bytes.

effect.description: §10.5: a selector is a bounded union of positive (allow) atoms plus explicit deny atoms; deny wins.

rule.description: One rule: a conjunction over the constrained domains. A rule matches a request when every constrained domain's request value is a member of the domain atom (allow rules require the request value to be present; deny rules conservatively match an absent request value — fail closed).

atoms.description: The closed twelve-domain atom table of §10.5, one optional constraint per domain. An omitted domain is unconstrained (top); an empty object is the universal rule. Unknown keys fail closed (additionalProperties false).

atomOperation.description: §10.5 operation row: 'Versioned BPP operation id; subset is set inclusion.' The atom is an explicit finite id set; an empty set matches nothing.

atomObject.description: §10.5 object/resource row: 'Exact source-qualified object id or server-expanded immutable collection snapshot; no mutable alias.' The AST carries only exact source-qualified ids; a pinned collection snapshot is server-expanded to exact ids at preparation with its transform id in the PreparationTrace (§10.5), so no mutable alias or unexpanded reference ever reaches the algebra. Subset is set inclusion.

atomPath.description: §10.5 path row: 'Unicode-normalized logical path segments relative to an exact WorkspaceAllocation root plus exact or subtree; string comparison never authorizes a filesystem open' (the owning broker enforces openat2-equivalent semantics at use). root is the exact WorkspaceAllocation ref; segments are NFC-normalized (evaluator-checked), never '.', '..', '/', or control characters. Different roots are disjoint. subtree covers the node and everything beneath it; exact covers only the node.

atomNetworkDestination.description: §10.5 network destination row: 'Scheme, A-label hostname or normalized IP/CIDR, port/range, and protocol; DNS resolution is pinned by the broker and private/special ranges require explicit atoms.' A DNS host and an IP/CIDR host are incomparable at policy level (the algebra never resolves names — typed reject); ip4 and ip6 forms are decidably disjoint. A CIDR with nonzero host bits below the prefix is not normalized and fails closed (evaluator-checked).

atomBinding.description: §10.5 provider/region/recipient row: 'Source-qualified immutable binding id; display names have no policy role.' Explicit finite set of exact binding ids; subset is set inclusion.

atomPurpose.description: §10.5 purpose row: 'Exact purpose ref or descendant in a pinned acyclic purpose snapshot.' snapshot pins the exact acyclic purpose snapshot (typed DigestRef); path is the materialized root-to-node ancestor chain from that snapshot (verified against the pin at preparation), so descendant testing is pure path-prefix comparison — no resolution inside the algebra. The atom covers the named node and its descendants; atoms over different snapshots are incomparable (typed reject).

atomClassification.description: §10.5 classification row: 'Element of a pinned finite lattice; restriction order is the lattice order.' lattice pins the exact finite lattice (typed DigestRef); allowed is the explicit downward-closed element set expanded against the pin at preparation (finite because the lattice is), so the lattice order is absorbed into set inclusion: subset is allowed ⊆ allowed, intersection is set intersection. Atoms over different lattices are incomparable (typed reject; §10.2 incomparable classification blocks derivation).

atomTime.description: §10.5 time row: 'Closed UTC server-time interval; a child interval must be contained.' Integer milliseconds of authoritative server time (§10.5: deadlines and expiry use authoritative server time); both endpoints inclusive; not_before <= not_after (evaluator-checked).

atomQuantity.description: §10.5 quantity row: 'Non-negative fixed-scale integer plus dimension and canonical unit; money additionally names ISO currency and pricing revision.' The atom is a ceiling: it covers integer amounts 0..max at the named fixed scale. Atoms differing in dimension, canonical_unit, scale, currency, or pricing_revision are incomparable (typed reject — §10.5: currency conversion and floating-point quantities reject); subset is max <= max; intersection is min(max).

atomRate.description: §10.5 rate row: 'Exact integer token-bucket RateCeiling and authority-server epoch; subset uses capacity/refill/burst containment.' Fields verbatim from the §10.5 RateCeiling record (integer discrete refill; clock is always authority_server). Atoms differing in dimension, canonical_unit, or epoch are incomparable (typed reject). Subset is the §10.5 containment: capacity <= capacity, max_burst <= max_burst, and refill-rate containment by exact integer cross-multiplication (child.refill_amount * parent.refill_period_milliseconds <= parent.refill_amount * child.refill_period_milliseconds — no floats). Worst-case boundary-alignment dominance beyond this containment is enforced at consume time by atomic ancestor-counter locking (§10.5) — ADR-0001 open item.

atomAssurance.description: §10.5 assurance row: 'Element of a pinned finite refinement order; incomparable profiles reject.' order pins the exact finite refinement order (typed DigestRef); admitted is the explicit upward-closed profile set expanded against the pin at preparation, so the refinement order is absorbed into set inclusion. Atoms over different orders are incomparable (typed reject); within one pinned order, profile-level incomparability is absorbed by the explicit-set expansion.

atomSchemaEvidence.description: §10.5 schema/evidence row: 'Exact immutable schema, verifier, attestor, and assurance-policy digests.' One exact digest tuple per atom (alternatives are separate rules); subset and intersection are exact tuple equality.

requestAtoms.description: The request side of decide(policy, request_atoms): one concrete value per supplied domain, compiled by the kernel from the dependency closure (§10.6), never caller-shaped. purpose reuses the atom shape (exact node = root-to-node path in the pinned snapshot); rate is the requested RateCeiling (matched by containment); schema_evidence is the exact offered digest tuple. An allow rule requires the constrained domain to be present and matching; a deny rule conservatively matches an absent domain (fail closed).

pointPath.description: Exact logical path relative to a WorkspaceAllocation root (§10.5 path row); authorization applies to the opened handle, never this string.

pointNetworkDestination.description: One concrete destination: exact host (A-label name or single broker-pinned IP), single port.

pointClassification.description: One element of the pinned finite lattice (§10.5 classification row); a different lattice pin is incomparable (typed reject).

pointTime.description: Authoritative server-time instant, integer milliseconds (§10.5 time row).

pointQuantity.description: One requested amount (§10.5 quantity row); mismatched dimension/unit/scale/currency/pricing revision is incomparable (typed reject — never converted).

pointAssurance.description: One attested profile in the pinned refinement order (§10.5 assurance row).

hostAtom.description: Exactly one closed host constructor: A-label DNS name, IPv4 CIDR, or IPv6 CIDR (§10.5 network destination row).

hostPoint.description: Exactly one concrete host: A-label DNS name or a single IP address.

ip4_cidr.description: Structured normalized IPv4 CIDR (no string parsing in the algebra); host bits below the prefix must be zero (evaluator-checked).

ip6_cidr.description: Structured normalized IPv6 CIDR as eight 16-bit groups; host bits below the prefix must be zero (evaluator-checked).

portRange.description: Inclusive port range; first <= last (evaluator-checked). A single port is first == last.

identifier.description: Opaque visible-ASCII identifier, at most 128 bytes (§14.9).

operationId.description: Versioned BPP operation id from the frozen bundle registry (§14.6).

sourceQualifiedId.description: Source-qualified immutable id: <source>:<id>, visible ASCII, one mandatory qualifier colon, at most 128 bytes total (§10.5: no mutable alias; display names have no policy role).

pathSegment.description: One logical path segment: never empty, '.', '..', and never containing '/' or control characters; NFC-normalized (evaluator-checked — §10.5 Unicode-normalized logical path segments).

aLabelHost.description: Lowercase A-label (punycode) hostname, LDH labels of at most 63 octets (§10.5: A-label hostname; no free text, no wildcard).

schemeOrProtocol.description: Exact lowercase scheme or protocol token (§10.5 network destination row); never a pattern.

dimensionOrUnit.description: Canonical dimension or unit token (§10.5 quantity/rate rows).

currencyCode.description: ISO 4217 alphabetic currency code (§10.5 money quantities name ISO currency).

timestampMs.description: Authoritative server time, integer milliseconds since the UTC epoch (§10.5; I-JSON safe integer, §14.2).

safeNonNegativeInteger.description: I-JSON safe integer (§14.2 rejects unsafe integers; §10.5 rejects floating-point quantities).

digestRef.$comment: The closed family DigestRef wire (family-vectors/PROFILE.md §6.1, normative; D-R0-1): exactly the members {class, algorithm, key_ref?, value_hex}. The oneOf pins the closed class/algorithm pairing and requires key_ref exactly for the keyed erasure classes; each arm refines members of this already-closed object.

class.description: Digest class (PROFILE.md §6, D-R0-1); substituting one class where a schema requires another is a conformance failure.

key_ref.description: Key id for the keyed erasure classes; raw HMAC keys, per-object secrets, and salts are never part of a DigestRef.

digestRef.description: Typed DigestRef pinning an immutable structure (lattice, purpose snapshot, refinement order, schema/verifier/attestor/assurance-policy): every digest field is typed, never an unlabelled hash. Atom comparability keys on exact DigestRef equality; the class is chosen per §14.2's digest-class table by the pinned structure's owner.

bpa1Policy.description: A BPA-1 policy value is a bounded set of rules; each rule is {effect: allow|deny, atoms} where atoms constrains a subset of the twelve closed §10.5 domains (an omitted domain is unconstrained; an empty atoms object is the universal rule). Deny wins; absence of a matching allow is deny (§10.5: a selector is a bounded union of positive atoms plus explicit deny atoms). The twelve domain keys are the ONLY atom keys (closed enum, ADR-0001 tag spellings frozen here): operation, object, path, network_destination, binding, purpose, classification, time, quantity, rate, assurance, schema_evidence — an unknown key is not extensible data, it fails closed; adding an atom type is BPA-2, never an in-place extension. Free text, regexes, shell syntax, display names, floats, mutable aliases, and implementation callbacks are not policy values (§10.5); all quantities are fixed-scale I-JSON safe integers. Canonical form (evaluator-enforced, policy/eval.py + policy/eval.mjs): set members sorted by UTF-16 code units, rules sorted by their JCS bytes, duplicates rejected; canonical bytes are RFC 8785 JCS and the policy digest is derived over the $domain-tagged canonical form with digest domain bpa1-policy-v1 (family-vectors/PROFILE.md §2, D-R0-1; the DigestRef class is chosen by the embedding record per §14.2). This schema is $domain-safe: every object is closed (additionalProperties false) and no property is named $domain. Cross-field rules JSON Schema cannot express are evaluator-checked and vector-pinned (spec/vectors/policy/): not_before <= not_after, ports.first <= ports.last, CIDR host bits zero below the prefix, NFC-normalized path segments, no duplicate set members. Bounds follow §14.9 (256 list items, 128-byte identifiers, bounded depth); the registry may re-pin them at bundle freeze.

ciphertextPublicDigest.description: Contextual digest-class binding (PROFILE.md §6.1/§6.2, D-R0-1; RT-02): the continuity state is a sealed blob the Society never reads — exactly class ciphertext_public (SHA-256 over the encrypted blob bytes) is acceptable; it is never a commitment to low-entropy plaintext, and any other class here is digest_class_mismatch.
